statement.name: Parallelization of well-foundedness / hyperjump
statement.definition: WF(T)=1 iff the tree T is well-founded; WF-hat is its parallelization, strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the hyperjump HJ, the analogue of Π11-CA0 (the catalogue only has chipi11, the single WF).
statement.facts: WF-hat ≡sW HJ (Lemma 3.6), ≡sW β-mod (Prop 3.12); HJ^n ≡sW HJ^[n] (Lemma 5.1); WF-hat is not Weihrauch reducible to Σ0α-RT for any α<ω1 (Cor 5.23).

statement.name: β-model function
statement.definition: Maps X to a pair (W,h) where W codes a countable β-model containing X and h is a Skolem function for Π01 predicates with parameters in W.
statement.facts: β-mod ≡sW WF-hat (Prop 3.12); it is a cylinder.

statement.notation: Γ-RT (Galvin–Prikry), Γ in {Σ0n, Π0n, Δ0n, Σ0α}
statement.name: Galvin-Prikry Ramsey property for Borel classes (problem and schema)
statement.definition: Γ-RT: given A in Γ([ω]^ω), find an infinite homogeneous set for A. The schema versions express that all Γ-definable sets of the Ramsey space are Ramsey.
statement.facts: Σ0k-RT ≤sW WF-hat^[k] (Lemma 5.4); Σ0_{k+1}-RT ≤W Σ0_k-RT ⋆ WF-hat (Lemma 5.5); Σ0_{k+1}-RT <W Σ01-RT ⋆ WF-hat^[k] (Cor 5.24); Σ01-RT ≤sW WF-hat (Cor 5.3); Π11-CA0 proves Σ0k-RT (Cor 2.11); RCA0+Δ02-RT proves Π11-CA0; Σ0_{ω+α}-RT ≤W Σ01-RT ⋆ HJ^{ω^{1+α}} (Prop 5.30); Σ0n-RT is a strictly increasing chain in arithmetical Weihrauch degrees; lightface Σ0_{k+1}/Δ0_{k+1} Galvin-Prikry equivalent over β-models to existence of HJ^k(∅) (Thm 6.1).

statement.name: One-sided and weak one-sided homogeneous set functions
statement.definition: FindHS_Γ(A)=HS(A)∩A on sets having a homogeneous set landing in A; wFindHS_Γ is its restriction to sets all of whose homogeneous sets land in A (catalogue has these only for Γ=Σ01, Π01, Δ01).
statement.facts: wFindHSΣ0_{k+1} ≡aW UC ⋆ WF-hat^[k]; wFindHSΠ0_{k+1} ≡aW C_{ω^ω} ⋆ WF-hat^[k] (Prop 5.13); wFindHSΣ0_{k+1} <aW wFindHSΠ0_{k+1}; WF-hat^[k] <aW wFindHSΔ0_{k+1} (Prop 5.10); wFindHSΠ0_{k+1} <W FindHSΠ0_{k+1} (Cor 5.28); Σ0_{k+1}-RT ≤aW FindHSΣ0_{k+1}; FindHSΣ0_{k+1} is not aW-below Σ01-RT ⋆ WF-hat^[k].

statement.name: Comparability of well-orderings (problems) and weak comparability
statement.definition: Given two well-orderings, produce an embedding of one onto an initial segment of the other (CWO), or an embedding of one into the other (WCWO).
statement.facts: WCWO ≤W CWO. CWO ≤W ATR (Prop. 4.5). ATR ≤W WCWO (Thm 6.3), so WCWO ≡W CWO ≡W ATR ≡W UCNN (Cor. 6.4), answering Marcone's question.

statement.name: Fraïssé's conjecture problems for linear orders and well-orderings, no infinite descending sequence, no infinite antichain
statement.definition: WQOLO and WQOWO: given a sequence of linear orders (well-orders), produce i<j and an embedding from Li into Lj. NDSWO: given well-orders and embeddings from Li+1 into Li, produce i<j and an embedding from Li into Lj. NIACWO: given well-orders, produce i, j (possibly i>j) and an embedding from Li into Lj.
statement.facts: NDSWO ≤W WQOWO ≤W WQOLO, and NIACWO ≤W WCWO ≤W CWO and NIACWO ≤W WQOWO. WQOWO ≤W ATR. ATR ≤W CN ∗ NDSWO and ATR ≤W CN ∗ NIACWO, hence ATR ≤c and ≤arith_W for each. ATR ≤c WQOLO. WQOLO ≤W CNN but CNN is not arithmetically W-reducible to WQOLO, and WQOLO is not computably or arithmetically W-reducible to UCNN. Open whether ATR ≤W NDSWO, NIACWO or WQOWO.

statement.name: Two-sided König duality theorem problem
statement.definition: Given a graph, produce an odd cycle or a König cover.
statement.facts: KDT2 ≤W LPO × KDT, hence KDT ≡W KDT2 (Prop. 9.5).

statement.name: Hindman's theorem for 2 colors
statement.definition: Hindman's theorem restricted to colorings of N with 2 colors.
statement.facts: Proposition III.43: HT2 implies HT over RCA0, by induction on the number of colors.

statement.name: Existence of right-matches, left-matches and full-matches
statement.definition: For every k-coloring c of N and infinite S there is a right-match (resp. left-match, full-match) (F,T) with F ∪ T ⊆ S, in the sense of Towsner's matches. RM_k, LM_k, FM_k are the versions with fixed k.
statement.facts: Theorem III.30 / Corollary III.30.2: right-matches exist computably in (c,S), uniformly in (c,S)'' (RCA0 proves Theorem III.11). Theorem III.40: no continuous functional maps a coloring to a right-match. Theorem III.41: every 2-coloring has a left-match computable uniformly in (c,S)''. Proposition III.44: RM_2 implies RM and FM_2 implies FM over RCA0. Corollary III.31.2: full-matches exist in ACA0. Whether every computable coloring has a computable full-match is open (Question III.54), as is whether LM_2 implies LM_k (Question III.45).

statement.notation: CSC space statements (T3 CSC metrizable, orderable, etc.)
statement.name: Topological characterization theorems for countable second countable spaces
statement.definition: Statements about countable second countable (CSC) topological spaces in Dorais's formalization: every regular eT2 CSC space is uniformly regular, T3 CSC space is metrizable or orderable, compact T2 CSC space is well-orderable, locally compact T2 CSC space has a choice of compact neighborhoods, T3 scattered CSC space has a Cantor-Bendixson rank, is completely metrizable, embeds into a well order, and so on.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, arithmetic comprehension is equivalent to many statements: every T3 eT2 CSC space is metrizable or has an algebra of clopen sets, every T3 CSC space is homeomorphic to a linear order, every compact CSC space is effectively compact. ACA0 proves every T3 CSC space is homeomorphic to a linear order and every compact T2 CSC space is homeomorphic to a well-order. Arithmetic transfinite recursion is equivalent over RCA0 to: every locally compact T2 CSC space has a choice of compact neighborhoods or is well-orderable, every T3 scattered CSC space embeds into a well order, has a Cantor-Bendixson rank, or is completely metrizable (Bel'nov-Knaster-Urbanik, Katetov), and to topological comparability of locally compact T2 CSC spaces. Π11 comprehension is equivalent over RCA0 to: the set of indices of compact, connected, scattered, or complete spaces exists; every T3 CSC space is ranked; every T3 CSC space splits into a scattered and a dense-in-itself subspace. The statements TAM and 1TAM about eventually well-founded tree arrays: TAM is equivalent to a statement about eventually well-ordered sequences of linear orders and is provable in ATR0, and 1TAM implies ATR0 over RCA0.

statement.notation: Σ¹₁-C_X, Σ¹₁-tree-C_X, Π⁰ₙ-C_{2^ω}, C_{2^ω}, C_{ω^ω} (Σ¹₁-presentation choice problems)
statement.name: Choice on analytic and arithmetical sets in Cantor/Baire space
statement.loc: Definition IV.11, Example IV.12, Theorems IV.13–IV.15
statement.definition: Given a presentation of a nonempty closed, Σ¹₁ or Π⁰ₙ set (or a Σ¹₁ tree), find an element or a path.
statement.facts: Σ¹₁-C_{ω^ω} ≡ Σ¹₁-tree-C_{ω^ω} ≡ C_{ω^ω} ≡ Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω} (IV.13). For n ≥ 2, C_{2^ω} ≡ Π⁰₁-C_{2^ω} <W Π⁰ₙ-C_{2^ω} ≡ Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω} (IV.14). C_{2^ω} <W Σ¹₁-WKL <W Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω} (IV.15).

statement.notation: Σ¹₁-UC_X, Σ¹₁-KC_X, Σ¹₁-C^fin, Σ¹₁-C^cof, Σ¹₁-C^foc, Σ¹₁-C^aof, Σ¹₁-C^aou, Σ¹₁-UC^tot
statement.name: Restricted Σ¹₁ single choice principles
statement.definition: Σ¹₁ choice restricted to singletons, compact, finite, cofinite, finite-or-cofinite, all-or-finite or all-or-unique sets. UC^tot is the totalization of unique choice.
statement.facts: Σ¹₁-UC_{ω^ω} <W Σ¹₁-KC_{ω^ω} ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL (IV.17). Parallelized Σ¹₁-C_2 ≡W Π¹₁-Tot2 ≡W Π¹₁-DNC2 (IV.18). Parallelized Σ¹₁-C^aou_N ≡W Π¹₁-Tot_N (IV.19). UC^tot_X ≡W C^aou_X for Δ¹₁ X (IV.27); parallelized Σ¹₁-UC^tot_2 ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL (IV.27.1).

statement.name: Π¹₁ totalization and diagonalization problems
statement.definition: Totalize a partial Π¹₁ function (2-valued or N-valued), or find a function diagonalizing a sequence of partial Π¹₁ functions.
statement.facts: Π¹₁-DNC_N ≤W Π¹₁-DNC2 ≡W Π¹₁-Tot2 ≤W Π¹₁-Tot_N, and the equivalences in IV.18 and IV.19.

statement.notation: Σ¹₁-AC_X, Σ¹₁-DC_X and restrictions Σ¹₁-AC^?_N, Σ¹₁-DC^?_N (? ∈ {fin, cof, foc, aof, aou})
statement.name: Σ¹₁ axioms of choice and dependent choice (Weihrauch problems)
statement.definition: AC is the parallelization of Σ¹₁ choice, giving an element of the product of nonempty Σ¹₁ sets. DC is the dependent version, giving a path through a Σ¹₁ tree of choices. The superscript restricts the type of sets.
statement.facts: Σ¹₁-DC_X ≡W Σ¹₁-tree-C_X (IV.22). Σ¹₁-AC_2 ≡W Σ¹₁-DC2 ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL <W Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω}, and Σ¹₁-AC_ω ≤W Σ¹₁-DC_ω ≡W Σ¹₁-C_{ω^ω} (IV.24). AC^fin ≡W DC^fin (IV.30). AC^aou ≡W AC^aof ≡W AC^fosc (IV.35.1). AC^aof ≡W DC^aof (IV.36.1). AC^fin <W AC^aof (IV.38.1). AC^cof is Weihrauch incomparable with AC^fin and AC^aof (IV.41.1). There are upward density and maximum Medvedev degree results (IV.31, IV.37, IV.42, IV.45.1) and downward density of Σ¹₁-DC_N (IV.46). Σ¹₁-ATR2 ≰W Σ¹₁-AC_ω (IV.100), hence Σ¹₁-AC_ω ≰W Σ¹₁-DC_ω (IV.100.1), answering Question IV.25.

statement.name: Weihrauch versions of ATR
statement.definition: ATR: given a well-order E and an arithmetical Φ, output a hierarchy for Φ on E. ATR2': like ATR2, but a jump hierarchy may be on an initial segment containing the well-founded part. ATR2^po: ATR2 for partial orders.
statement.facts: ATR ≡W Σ¹₁-UC_{ω^ω} (IV.76). ATR <W ATR2' ≤W ATR2 ≤W ATR2^po (IV.72). ATR2^po <W C_{ω^ω} (IV.77). Parallelized ATR2' ≡aW Σ¹₁-KC_{N^N} ≡aW parallelized Σ¹₁-C^aou_N (IV.65). Σ¹₁-C^aou_N ≤W ATR2^po (IV.69). Robustness results (IV.61, IV.63) are cited from Goh.

statement.name: Unbounded ATR and method of pseudo-hierarchies
statement.definition: Given an arithmetical Φ and a halting condition Ψ, find an ordinal and a hierarchy satisfying Ψ. For MPH, the alternative is an ill-founded order with a pseudo-hierarchy that never satisfies Ψ.
statement.facts: MPH is equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (IV.58, IV.59). ATR2 <W ATRunb and ATR2^po <W ATRunb (IV.73). C_{ω^ω} ≤W MPH and C_{ω^ω} ≤W ATRunb (IV.78). PTT_det ≤W ATRunb (IV.83). It is open whether ATRunb ≡W MPH (Question IV.75).

statement.name: Weihrauch-problem versions of ATR0-level theorems
statement.definition: PTT_list: enumerate a superset of [T]. PTT_det: a perfect subtree or an enumeration covering [T]. CWO: compare two well-orders by an embedding onto an initial segment. WCWO: embedding not necessarily onto an initial segment. Σ¹₁-Sep: separate two disjoint Σ¹₁-described sets of N.
statement.facts: ATR ≡W Σ¹₁-Sep <W Π¹₁-Sep ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL (IV.80, cited). ATR ≡W PTT_list <W PTT_1 <W PTT_det (IV.82, cited). CWO ≡W ATR ≡W WCWO (IV.85, cited).

statement.name: Laver Partition Theorem for open (resp. clopen) sets
statement.definition: For every open (resp. clopen) set A ⊆ ω^ω there is a Laver tree T' with empty stem such that [T'] ⊆ A or [T'] ∩ A = ∅. Also considered as problems whose solutions are codes of Laver trees.
statement.facts: Σ01-RT implies LLΣ01 and Δ01-RT implies LLΔ01 over RCA0 (Lemma 1.1). Σ01-DET implies LLΣ01 over RCA0 (Lemma 1.2). LLΔ01 implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Lemma 4.1). RCA0 + finitary Σ11-AC0 + LLΔ01 proves Δ11-CA0 (Prop. 4.5). RCA0 + finitary Σ11-AC0 + LLΣ01 proves Σ11-AC0 (Prop. 4.6). Over RCA0 + Σ11-IND, LLΔ01 implies Δ11-CA0 and LLΣ01 implies Σ11-AC0 (Thm 1.7). LLΔ01 ≡sW UC_{ω^ω} (Thm 5.3). TC_{ω^ω} ≤W C_{2^ω} ⋆ LLΣ01 (Lemma 5.12). TC_{ω^ω} <aW LLΣ01 (Prop. 5.15). LLΣ01 ≰W C_{ω^ω} (Cor. 5.13). Computability bounds: Thm 1.9, Thm 1.10, Cor. 3.4, Cor. 3.5.

statement.name: Hechler–Laver principles
statement.definition: For every open set A there is either a Hechler tree T with [T] ⊆ A or a Laver tree S with [S] ∩ A = ∅ (HLΣ01). The dual version for Π01 is HLΠ01, and HLΔ01 is the analogous clopen version.
statement.facts: ATR0 proves HLΣ01 and HLΠ01 (Thm 1.5, Thm 3.2). Over RCA0, ATR0 is equivalent to HLΔ01 (and HLΣ01, HLΠ01) (Thm 1.8, Lemma 4.4). HLΣ01 or HLΠ01 implies LLΣ01, and HLΔ01 implies LLΔ01.

statement.name: Find-Laver-tree problems
statement.definition: Given A ∈ Γ(ω^ω), find a code of a Laver tree T with [T] ⊆ A. The domain of FindL is the A for which such a tree exists; the domain of wFindL is the A meeting every Laver tree.
statement.facts: wFindLΔ01, wFindLΣ01, LLΔ01, FindLΔ01 and FindLΣ01 are all ≡sW UC_{ω^ω} (Thm 5.3). FindLΠ01 ≡sW C_{ω^ω} (Prop. 5.4). C_{2^ω} ⋆ wFindLΠ01 ≡W C_{ω^ω} (Prop. 5.5). wFindLΠ01 is not a cylinder, hence wFindLΠ01 ≢sW FindLΠ01 (Thm 5.10). wFindLΠ01 is parallelizable (Prop. 5.11).

statement.name: Finitary Σ11 choice
statement.definition: The schema ∀i ∃f φ(i,f) → ∀n ∃g ∀i ≤ n φ(i, g_i) for Σ11 formulas φ.
statement.facts: Implied over RCA0 by both Σ11-AC0 and Σ11-IND (Lemma 2.7). Used as a base theory for partial reversals.

statement.name: Closed choice on a represented space X
statement.definition: Given a nonempty closed subset of X by negative information (an enumeration of its complement), find a point of it.
statement.facts: Characterizes the classes of computable functions (X={0}), finitely many mind changes (X=N), weakly computable functions (X Cantor space), and effectively Borel measurable functions (X Baire space). C_{N×{0,1}^N} ≡W C_R. Proves C_Q ≡W C_N, C_{R\Q} ≡W C_{N^N}. Choice on Polish spaces falls into the dichotomy C_R-below or C_{N^N}-equivalent. Also: C_{{0,1}}×C_{{0,1}} <W C_{{0,1}×{0,1}}.

statement.name: Low representation / low computability operator
statement.definition: Single-valued map on Baire space whose computable inputs yield exactly the low points.
statement.facts: f is low computable iff f ≤sW L (Theorem 8.10). C_{{0,1}^N} ≤sW L; C_{N×{0,1}^N} ≤sW L and L ≰W C_{N×{0,1}^N}. L <W lim. L <W L×L, so L is not idempotent. Composition of a low computable map with a limit computable map is limit computable.

statement.name: Limit with respect to the initial topology of the jump (Π-topology)
statement.definition: lim_J = J^{-1}∘lim∘J^N, the limit operator on Baire space with respect to the initial topology of the Turing jump J.
statement.facts: lim_J <sW L, and lim_J ≡sW L relative to some oracle. C_{{0,1}^N} ≰W lim_J. lim_∆ <W lim_J <W lim. Points limit computable in the jump are low and do not bound DNC functions.

statement.name: Discrete limit
statement.definition: Limit of eventually constant sequences in Baire space.
statement.facts: lim_∆ ≡W C_N (Corollary 7.12); f ≤W lim_∆ iff f is computable with finitely many mind changes.

statement.name: Stable Ramsey theorem restricted to unbalanced colourings
statement.definition: SRT^2_k restricted to colourings such that all infinite homogeneous sets have the same colour.
statement.facts: TC_N, Sort and LPO' are each ≤_W u-SRT^2_2. u-SRT^2_k ≤_W lim' (indeed ≤_W lim_k ∗ lim). C_ℓ'' ≰_W u-SRT^2_k, so 1 u-SRT^2_k <_W 1 SRT^2_k.

statement.name: Hausdorff dimension of closed subsets of [0,1] (resp. as upper real)
statement.definition: The map A ↦ dim_H(A) from closed subsets of [0,1] to R, and the variant dim_H^> with output type R>.
statement.facts: dim_H ≡W lim ⋆ lim and dim_H^> ≡W lim (Theorem 48). Corollary 53: there is a computable closed and computably overt set whose Hausdorff dimension is Turing-equivalent to ∅''.

statement.name: Maximal flow on the infinite binary tree
statement.definition: Given a non-negative edge assignment f on the full binary tree, find a flow g ≤ f with g(ε) maximal.
statement.facts: MaxFlow ≡W lim.

statement.name: Non-zero flow
statement.definition: Given an edge assignment f, find a flow g ≤ f with g(ε) > 0.
statement.facts: NonZeroFlow ≡W C_N × C_{0,1}^N (≡ C_N × WKL) (Theorem 39), which is ≡W C_R (Corollary 57).

statement.name: Construct a measure supported in a closed set
statement.definition: Given a non-empty closed A ⊆ X, find a non-zero measure µ with supp(µ) ⊆ A.
statement.facts: ConstructMeasure_X ≡W C_X for a computable Polish space X (Theorem 34). ConstructMeasure[0,1] <W supp^{-1} (Corollary 35). ConstructMeasure[0,1] ≡W C[0,1] ≡W H1 C[0,1] (Figure 1).

statement.name: Support of a measure and inverse
statement.definition: supp maps a measure to its support (as overt set, or as closed set); supp^{-1} constructs a measure with a given closed set as support.
statement.facts: supp : M(X) → V(X) is computable. For X perfect (or with a computable embedding of N) and effectively locally compact, supp^A_X ≡W (supp^A_X)^{-1} ≡W lim (relative to the Halting problem otherwise).

statement.name: Frostman measure constructions
statement.definition: Given a closed A ⊆ [0,1] and s, find an s-Frostman measure supported in A (resp. with support exactly A).
statement.facts: Frost ≡W C_N × C[0,1] ≡W NonZeroFlow (Corollary 57); StrictFrost ≡W lim ≡W MaxFlow (Corollary 58).

statement.name: Closed choice on sets of positive Hausdorff dimension (resp. dimension 1)
statement.definition: Restriction of C[0,1] to closed sets of positive Hausdorff dimension, resp. dimension 1.
statement.facts: HC[0,1] ≡W H1 C[0,1] ≡W C[0,1] (via Shmerkin's construction).

statement.name: Perfect core and concentrated-measure operations
statement.definition: PerfectCore maps a closed set A to a closed and overt B ⊇ A with the same perfect kernel; Concentrate produces a concentrated non-atomic measure below a given one; ConcentratedSupport computes the support of a concentrated measure as closed and overt.
statement.facts: All three are computable.

statement.name: Upper bound for monotone bounded sequence of naturals
statement.definition: Given a monotone bounded sequence of naturals, find an upper bound.
statement.facts: Used to show WKL × UpperBound ≤W NonZeroFlow.

statement.name: (Induced) subgraph decision problems
statement.definition: For a computable graph G, IS_G(H)=1 iff G is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of H, and S_G(H)=1 iff G is isomorphic to a subgraph of H. The e-versions take graphs given by enumerations as input.
statement.facts: For finite G, LPO ≡sW S_G ≡sW IS_G, and for G not a complete graph LPO' ≡sW eIS_G (Theorem 3.17). For infinite c.e. G with R ⊑s G, or with K_ω not induced in G, the problems are ≡sW WF (Lemmas 3.18, 3.19), so there is no c.e. G with LPO <W IS_G <W WF (Theorem 3.20). For the trees T_{2k+1} and forests F_{2k+2}, S_G is ≡sW LPO^(2k) resp. LPO^(2k+1) (parallelized), by Theorem 3.22.

statement.name: (Induced) subgraph search problems
statement.definition: Given a graph H containing G as a (induced) subgraph, output a (induced) subgraph of H isomorphic to G. There are four variants (χχ, χe, eχ, ee) according to whether input and output graphs are given by characteristic function or by enumeration.
statement.facts: These problems are cylinders (Prop. 4.2) and are bounded above by C_NN (Prop. 4.3). IS-Copy_G ≡W C_NN, possibly relative to an oracle (Thm 4.5). S-Copy_G ≡W C_NN when G has only finitely many vertices of finite degree (Thm 4.6) and for G ∈ {L, C_n ⊔ R, K_m ⊔ R, 2^{<N}} (Prop. 4.14). S-Copy_G is computable for finite G (Thm 4.4) and for certain disjoint unions of finite graphs (Thm 4.39). IS-Copy of the disjoint union of all C_i (i≥3) is ≡W C_NN (Thm 4.40). S-Copy_R <W C_NN, and C_NN ≡W lim^2 ⋆ S-Copy_R (Cor. 4.16). S-Copy_R is incomparable with lim in some variants (Thm 4.18). The first-order part of S-Copy_R is that of C_NN (Prop. 4.17). S-Copy_{F_{2k+2}} ≤W the parallelization of LPO^(2k-1) (Thm 4.44).

statement.name: Ray embedding problem
statement.definition: Given a graph H isomorphic to G, where R ⊑s G, find a sequence p such that (p(i), p(i+1)) is an edge of H for every i.
statement.facts: These problems are cylinders (Prop. 4.11) and are ≤W C_NN (Lemma 4.12). R-Emb_R ≡W eR-Emb_R ≡W lim^2 (Prop. 4.15). R-Emb_G ⋆ S-Copy_R ≡W C_NN (Prop. 4.13).

statement.name: Strong Σ¹ₙ dependent choice
statement.definition: For η in Σ¹ₙ: ∃Z ∀n (∃Y η(n,(Z)<n,Y) → η(n,(Z)<n,(Z)n)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ¹ₙ-Rfn over ACA0 (Thm 3.1).

statement.notation: Categoricity of DLO, random graph, atomless Boolean algebras
statement.name: Countable categoricity principles
statement.definition: Any two countable dense linear orders without endpoints (resp. random graphs, atomless Boolean algebras) are isomorphic, with the inverse isomorphism also existing.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to RCA0 over PRA2.

statement.notation: IntermediateValueTheorem, Completeness of R, HeineBorelTheorem (problem forms)
statement.name: Problem forms of analysis theorems
statement.definition: Instances are presentations of functions, Cauchy sequences, or covers of [0,1] by rational open intervals. Solutions are a point where the function is discontinuous or zero, the limit, or an uncovered point.
statement.facts: Over PRA2, HeineBorelTheorem is equivalent to WKL0 (Proposition 6.5). IntermediateValueTheorem is conjectured to be equivalent to Δ⁰₁-CA over PRA2 (Proposition 5.8). For each of these, every computable instance has a primitive recursive instance whose solutions compute a solution (Theorem 5.4).

statement.name: Baer type problem
statement.definition: Given a Baer categorical rank 1 torsion-free abelian group, output its Baer type, i.e. the set {m : m | g} for a nonzero g.
statement.facts: Every c.e. degree is the degree of the solutions of some computable instance. The only primitive recursive instance is the trivial group (Proposition 5.11).

statement.notation: Szpilrajn, graph reorientation, Rival–Sands for honest graphs, Hall's theorem variants, connected components
statement.name: Combinatorial principles done in PRA2
statement.definition: Szpilrajn's theorem; transitive reorientation of pseudo-transitive oriented graphs; Rival–Sands and (2n-1)-colouring for honestly presented locally finite graphs; Hall's theorem for finite A or under the extended Hall condition; existence of connected components.
statement.facts: The first four are proved in PRA2 (Propositions 3.11–3.13). Existence of connected components, under the hypothesis that finitely many vertices have every vertex connected to one of them, is equivalent to 2^N-RCA0 over PRA2 (Proposition 3.14).

statement.name: k-colorability of locally k-colorable graphs
statement.definition: Every locally k-colorable graph is k-colorable.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 for every k ≥ 2 (Hirst, cited).

statement.name: Colorability of locally ℓ-colorable graphs with k colors
statement.definition: COL(ℓ,k,G) says: if G is a locally ℓ-colorable graph then G is k-colorable. The two principles quantify k uniformly over G and non-uniformly, respectively.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.2 (cited from Hirst), 5.3 (Gasarch–Hirst) and 5.4 (Schmerl): for fixed standard k ≥ ℓ ≥ 2, WKL is equivalent over RCA0 to every locally ℓ-colorable graph being k-colorable. Theorem 5.7: ∀ℓ∃k∀G COL+BΣ02 does not prove WKL. Theorem 5.8: ∀ℓ∀G∃k COL+BΣ02 does not prove ∃k∀f DNR(k,f). Proposition 6.1: RCA0+BΣ02 does not prove ∀k(∀f DNR(k,f) → ∀G COL(k,2k−1,G)).

statement.name: Prediction statement of Schmerl
statement.definition: There is an X with Σ01(X)-definable sets N=D0⊇...⊇Dn and Σ01(X)-definable functions Hi: Di+1→k such that every family of Σ01(Y)-definable functions Fj: Dj→k agrees with the Hi at some common point x in Dn.
statement.facts: Predict_1(k) essentially says ∃f ¬DNR(k,f). Proposition 6.8: if Predict_n(k) holds and Adam has a winning strategy in the on-line coloring game, then some graph in the natural class is not k-colorable. Corollary 6.11: Predict_{f(k)}(k) implies there is a locally 2-colorable graph that is not k-colorable.

statement.name: Limit operation with respect to the jump topology
statement.definition: lim restricted to sequences that converge in the jump topology.
statement.facts: BCT_0′ ≤sW lim_J, and BCT_0′ <W lim_J. lim_J is not probabilistic (Corollary 9.8).

statement.name: Atsuji spaces (every continuous function on the space is uniformly continuous)
statement.definition: A complete separable metric space A is Atsuji if every continuous function from A to an arbitrary complete separable metric space B is uniformly continuous.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0: every Lebesgue space is Atsuji (Thm 6.1). Provable in ACA0: every Atsuji space is Lebesgue (Thm 6.7); the paper does not know whether ACA0 is needed. Over WKL0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every perfect Atsuji space is compact' (Thm 4.3). Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'every compact space is Atsuji' and to '[0,1] is Atsuji' (Thm 4.1), and also to 'there exists a perfect Atsuji space' (Lemma 4.5). Heine-Borel compact spaces are Atsuji in RCA0 (Lemma 4.2).

statement.name: Lebesgue spaces (every open covering has a Lebesgue number)
statement.definition: A complete separable metric space A is Lebesgue if for every open covering U of A there is q>0 such that every ball B(x,q) is contained in some member of U.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to '[0,1] is Lebesgue' (Thm 5.5). Heine-Borel compact spaces are Lebesgue in RCA0 (Lemma 5.3). Every perfect Lebesgue space is Heine-Borel compact in RCA0 (Thm 5.4). Over WKL0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every perfect Lebesgue space is compact' (Thm 5.6). Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'there exists a perfect Lebesgue space' (Lemma 5.7).

statement.name: Compactness notions in weak subsystems
statement.definition: Compact: there is a sequence of finite 2^-n-nets of the space. Heine-Borel compact: every open covering has a finite subcovering.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'every compact space is Heine-Borel compact' (Thm 3.4, Brown/Simpson). Over WKL0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every Heine-Borel compact space is compact' and also to the version restricted to perfect spaces (Thm 3.6). Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'there is a perfect Heine-Borel compact space' (Lemma 3.8).

statement.name: Continuity of the distance function from a closed set
statement.definition: For every closed set C there is a continuous function f_C(x)=inf{d(x,y): y in C}; variants say that {(x,e): B(x,e) is not contained in U} is open.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to Π¹₁-CA0 (Thm 7.1). The version for separably closed sets is equivalent to ACA0 (Thm 7.3).

statement.name: Closed versus separably closed sets (Brown)
statement.definition: A separably closed set is the closure of a coded sequence of points; a closed set is the complement of a coded open set.
statement.facts: Cited from Brown: over RCA0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every separably closed set is closed'. Π¹₁-CA0 is equivalent to 'every closed set is separably closed'.

statement.name: Layer function for a universal Martin-Löf test
statement.definition: LAY_U : MLR ⇒ N with n ∈ LAY_U(p) iff p ∉ U_n; its degree does not depend on the universal test U.
statement.facts: LAY ≡W RD ≡W C_N × d_MLR (Theorem 3.3). LAY×LAY ≡W LAY and LAY⋆LAY ≡W LAY (Cor. 3.4). LAY <W C_N (Cor. 3.5). LAY⋆C_N ≡W C_N⋆LAY ≡W LAY (Cor. 3.6). LAY <W LAY-hat ≡W lim × d_MLR (Cor. 3.7). LAY <W LAY* ≡W id ⊔ LAY <W C_N (Cor. 3.8). A function f is ≤W LAY iff it is effectively Δ⁰₂-measurable iff Π⁰₁-piecewise computable (Cor. 3.10). Every layerwise computable f satisfies f ≤W LAY (Obs. 3.2).

statement.name: Randomness deficiency function
statement.definition: RD_U : MLR → N, RD_U(p) = min{n : p ∉ U_n}.
statement.facts: RD ≡W LAY ≡W C_N × d_MLR (Theorem 3.3).

statement.name: Kolmogorov randomness deficiency
statement.definition: Kol(p) = min{c : ∀n K(p≤n) ≥ n − c}, for p ∈ MLR.
statement.facts: Kol ≡W C_N × d_MLR (Proposition 3.11).

statement.name: Law of the iterated logarithm (effective, multivalued)
statement.definition: LIL : MLR ⇒ N with N ∈ LIL(α) iff for all n ≥ N, |Σ_{i<n}(2α(i)−1)| < sqrt(2n log log n).
statement.facts: LIL ≡W LAY (Theorem 4.8).

statement.name: Toy Birkhoff theorem convergence rate
statement.definition: Birkhoff : MLR × N ⇒ N with N ∈ Birkhoff(p,k) iff for all n ≥ N the average of π1(S^i(p)) for i ≤ n differs from 1/2 by less than 2^{-k}.
statement.facts: Birkhoff ≡W LAY (Theorem 4.10). The general convergence rate in Birkhoff's ergodic theorem is not layerwise computable.

statement.name: Random harmonic series
statement.definition: The map sending p ∈ MLR to Σ_n (−1)^{p(n)}/n ∈ R.
statement.facts: It is layerwise computable (Dai) and ≡W LAY (Theorem 4.12).

statement.name: Approximate sum comparison for random harmonic series
statement.definition: SumApr : MLR × Q × N ⇒ {0,1} with 0 ∈ SumApr(p,q,k) if the random harmonic sum is < q + 2^{-k}, and 1 ∈ SumApr(p,q,k) if the sum is > q.
statement.facts: Layerwise computable, not computable, and not Weihrauch-complete for layerwise computability.

statement.name: Kleene star of LPO
statement.definition: LPO* is defined by f^0 = id, f^{n+1} = f^n × f, f*(n,x) = f^n(x), applied to LPO.
statement.facts: (min :⊆ A(N)→N) ≡W LPO* (cited from Mylatz [25]; the text writes O(N)). LPO* <W C_N even relative to any oracle (cited from [29]).

statement.name: Overt choice on a represented space X
statement.definition: VC_X :⊆ V(X) ⇒ X takes a non-empty closed set A, given by positive information about which open sets intersect it (an element of V(X)), and returns a point of A.
statement.facts: VC_X is computable for precomputable quasi-Polish X (Theorem 20). For countably-based T1 spaces, VC_X is continuous iff X is quasi-Polish (Corollary 23). For coanalytic separable metric spaces, VC_X is continuous iff X is Polish (Corollary 36). VC_X × VC_Y ≤sW VC_{X×Y} (Corollary 10). VC_X ≤W Π02 C_X' for a computable surjection X' → X (Proposition 31). For effectively countably-based X, any f :⊆ {0,1}^N ⇒ N with f ≤W VC_X is computable (Proposition 28). So C_N ≰W VC_X unless VC_X is computable (Corollary 30 for homogeneous spaces gives incomparability with C_N). Overt choice on a CoPolish space is continuous iff the space is countably-based. For Fréchet-Urysohn CoPolish X, VC_X ≤tW LPO (Theorem 60) and ACC_m ≰W VC_X (Theorem 63). For non-Fréchet-Urysohn T1 X, LPO ≤tW VC_X (Theorem 64), and VC_X ≤W (id: ΣΠ11 → Σ) for CoPolish X (Theorem 67). Corollary 68 gives a trichotomy for CoPolish spaces.

statement.name: Overt choice on the rationals
statement.definition: Overt choice VC_X for X = Q, the Euclidean rationals as a subspace of R.
statement.facts: VC_Q ≡W ECP (Proposition 39). It is not computable (Proposition 38). VC_Q |W C_N ≡W C_Q (Corollary 40). VC_Q ≰W C_R (Corollary 41). VC_Q ≡W VC_Q* (Corollary 35). HitSparse <W VC_Q (Corollary 44). Open: is it reducible to lim or to Sort?

statement.name: Overt choice on the space S0
statement.definition: Overt choice on S0, the set of finite sequences of naturals with the topology generated by the sets {u | u ⋠ w}.
statement.facts: FSL ≤W VC_S0 (Proposition 47). FSL <W VC_S0 (Corollary 48). VC_S0 ≡W VC_S0* (Corollary 35). Open: relation to VC_Q, lim and Sort.

statement.name: Overt choice on the CoPolish Fréchet-Urysohn space Tmin
statement.definition: Overt choice on the space Tmin with underlying set N^2 ∪ {∞}, a Fréchet-Urysohn CoPolish space that is not countably-based.
statement.facts: ACC_N ≤sW VC_Tmin (Proposition 57). Hence VC_Tmin is not computable or continuous.

statement.name: Overt choice on the CoPolish non-Fréchet-Urysohn space Smin
statement.definition: Overt choice on the space Smin on {(∞,∞)} ∪ (N×{∞}) ∪ N^2, a CoPolish space that is not Fréchet-Urysohn.
statement.facts: VC_Smin ≡W LPO (Theorem 66). The reduction LPO ≤sW VC_Smin is strong.

statement.name: Eventually constant path
statement.definition: Given an enumeration of a non-empty tree T ⊆ {0,1}* in which every vertex extends to an eventually constant path, find an eventually constant path.
statement.facts: ECP is not computable (Proposition 38). ECP ≡W VC_Q (Proposition 39).

statement.name: Finite sequence leaf
statement.definition: Given an enumeration of a non-empty tree with a leaf below every vertex, find a leaf, as an element of the space S{0,1}* of finite sequences.
statement.facts: FSL is not computable (Proposition 46). FSL ≤W VC_S0 and FSL ≤W C_N. FSL <W VC_S0.

statement.name: Hit sparse
statement.definition: Given an infinite A ⊆ N (as a closed set, by negative information) and f: N → N, find an open set U meeting A with |[n,f(n)] ∩ U| ≤ 1 for all n.
statement.facts: HitSparse is not computable, and HitSparse ≤W VC_Q (Theorem 43, due to Brattka). HitSparse ≤W C_N. HitSparse <W VC_Q (Corollary 44).

statement.name: Closed choice on the rationals
statement.definition: Closed choice C_X for X = Q.
statement.facts: C_Q ≡W C_N (Proposition 26). If f :⊆ X ⇒ Q satisfies f ≤W C_R then f ≤W C_N (Corollary 27).

statement.name: All-or-co-unique choice on {0,...,m-1}
statement.definition: ACC_m is the problem of finding an element of a closed set from {M, M \ {i} | i ∈ N}, where M = {0,...,m-1}.
statement.facts: ACC_2 ≡W LLPO. ACC_m ≰W VC_X for admissibly represented Fréchet-Urysohn X and m ≥ 2 (Theorem 63).

statement.name: Extension Auslander-Ellis theorem
statement.definition: Given a compact system (X1,T1) with points x1,y1 satisfying the conclusion of AET and a second system (X2,T2) with x2, there is y2 such that (y1,y2) is uniformly recurrent and proximal to (x1,x2) in the product system.
statement.facts: Follows from adaptations of classical proofs of AET; implies eAET'; strength unknown (Question 1). ACA_0^omega+(mu)+(Umin) proves eAET'; ACA_0^omega+(mu)+IHT+(Umin) is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA_0+eAET; eAET proves that every finite partition of a central set contains a central set.

statement.name: Refinement eAET' of the Auslander-Ellis theorem
statement.definition: For each n and each sequence of continuous i-ary functions t_i : X^i -> X (i<n), there is (y_i)_{i<n} uniformly recurrent in the n-fold product and proximal to (t_0, t_1(y_0), ..., t_{n-1}(y_0,...,y_{n-2})).
statement.facts: Implied by eAET; ACA_0^omega+(mu)+(Umin) proves eAET' (Theorem 16); ACA_0^omega+(mu)+IHT+(Umin) is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA_0+eAET' (Corollary 15); strength unknown.

statement.notation: partial minimal idempotent ultrafilter for countable algebras
statement.name: Existence of partial minimal idempotent ultrafilters on countable algebras
statement.definition: For every countable (downward translation) algebra there is a partial non-principal ultrafilter F satisfying idempotency (*) and minimality (†).
statement.facts: For arbitrary countable algebras, existence of partial non-principal (resp. minimal) ultrafilters is equivalent to ACA_0 over RCA_0. For downward translation algebras, existence of partial minimal idempotent ultrafilters, of partial idempotent ultrafilters, and of almost downward translation invariant ultrafilters are each equivalent to AET and IHT over ACA_0.

statement.name: Existence of a minimal idempotent ultrafilter (higher-order)
statement.definition: There is a higher-order object U of type 2 that is a non-principal, idempotent, minimal ultrafilter on N, respecting coding of sets.
statement.facts: ACA_0^omega+(mu)+IHT+(Umin) is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA_0+eAET (Theorem 14); the statement forall f exists U minimal idempotent extending tF(f) proves eAET over ACA_0^omega+(mu) (Theorem 18).
